Prevention: Use certified delinted cotton seed to reduce the chance of contamination.
Seeds are spread by animals - do not allow livestock into an affected area to avoid spread.
Seeds stick on clothes and shoes - remove seeds when leaving an infested area to prevent spreading.
Seed is spread by water - avoid runoff from surrounding infested fields by constructing contour bunds.
Prevent spread of blackjack by slashing or mowing before it flowers.
The seed is spread by wind - erect wind breaks around the fields by planting
Monitoring: Annual erect broadleaved weed (up to 1m high) with green compound leaves and a strong taproot.
Flowers white with yellow centre and 1cm long black seeds with 2-4 yellowish awns at one end.
Regularly (fortnightly) check surroundings for presence of weed along water bodies, pathways, fields.
Check fields for infestation and consider direct control as soon as weeds appear.
Check for flowering and seed development to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank.
Direct Control: Weed or hand pull plants prior to onset of flowering, ensuring the taproot is severed well below the crown to prevent regrowth.
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
